Subject: Dedicated capacity — session-pulse & GPU-mix checklist

Hi Hector —

Thanks for the quick intake last week. Before we size a Dedicated pool for OrchidAI, can you confirm the details below? Having the traffic pulse and a short sample of real prompts will let us recommend a GPU mix and a burst plan that balances cost and tail latency.

Key asks (short answers are fine):
- Average sustained qps and expected 95th/99th percentile peak qps (local timezone/dayparting)
- Typical prompt token length (min/median/max) and typical response token length
- Fraction of requests that use streaming vs batch (approx %)
- Session/pinning behavior: do sessions keep KV cache warm across requests? Typical session duration and requests/session
- Concurrency model: number of concurrent users vs concurrent inference sessions (if different)
- Burst profile: longest burst duration you expect and how often (daily/weekly/monthly)
- SLOs: target p95 latency and any hard p99 guardrails
- Fallback tolerances: acceptable model fallback (smaller quantized variant?) and maximum % of calls that can be degraded during capacity pressure
- Security/region constraints: need for dedicated VPC or specific KMS/HSM?

If you can attach a 24–72h token-level sample (CSV is fine) and 5–10 example prompts, we’ll run a quick probe and propose a recommended pool (GPU SKUs, oversubscription factor, prefix cache strategy) and a canary plan.

I attached a template you can drop the sample into.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through if that’s easier.

— Camila

Camila — thanks, attaching a short export. See answers inline below and in the CSV.

On Tue, Oct 19, 2027 at 09:12 AM Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Key asks (short answers are fine):
> - Average sustained qps and expected 95th/99th percentile peak qps (local timezone/dayparting)

Average sustained QPS: ~45 qps globally (Europe + US, US peak window 09:00–11:00 PT).
95th/99th peak QPS (US peak): 180 qps / 280 qps.

> - Typical prompt token length (min/median/max) and typical response token length

Prompt tokens: min 8 / median 64 / max 540
Response tokens: min 16 / median 128 / max 1024

> - Fraction of requests that use streaming vs batch (approx %)

About 30% streaming (progressive responses), 70% non-streaming.

> - Session/pinning behavior: do sessions keep KV cache warm across requests? Typical session duration and requests/session

Yes — we keep sessions alive for ~6–8 minutes on average; requests/session ~3–6. KV reuse is high (estimated reuse ~65%).

> - Concurrency model: number of concurrent users vs concurrent inference sessions (if different)

Concurrent end-users at US peak ~1,200, concurrent inference sessions ~850 (some sessions fan out).

> - Burst profile: longest burst duration you expect and how often (daily/weekly/monthly)

Longest continuous burst: ~9 minutes, ~3x sustained traffic. High-intensity events ~monthly.

> - SLOs: target p95 latency and any hard p99 guardrails

Target p95 (inference): 180ms; p99 goal < 600ms — hard requirement is p99 < 1000ms.

> - Fallback tolerances: acceptable model fallback (smaller quantized variant?) and maximum % of calls that can be degraded during capacity pressure

We can tolerate up to 12% fallback to a quantized gpt-variant for non-critical queries. For critical paths (payments, fraud checks) we need full model fidelity.

> - Security/region constraints: need for dedicated VPC or specific KMS/HSM?

Require VPC and bring-your-own-KMS for production; dev/test can be in Redwood hosted.

Uploading: orchid_traffic_snapshot.csv (24h token-level sample). Let me know if you want a longer window.

— Hector

Thanks for the data, Hector — this is very helpful. Quick read and recommendations:

- Given sustained 45 qps and US peak p99 of 280 qps with high KV reuse (65%), a mixed pool looks appropriate: a majority of 80GB GPU SKUs (for large context requests) plus a small set of denser 32GB SKUs for cost-effective handling of median/shorter prompts.
- Suggest starting with a 6:2 ratio (80GB:32GB) sized to provide ~1.5x headroom over expected US peak to keep p99 well under 800ms during 9-minute bursts.
- For streaming traffic (~30%), we can prioritize instances with lower per-token latency — we’ll route streaming to the 80GB pool where context switching is cheaper.
- Autoscaling policy: baseline autoscale target at 70% occupancy, aggressive scale up at 85% sustained across the cluster for >60s, and a cooldown to avoid oscillation.
- Canary: 10% traffic on day 1 of conversion, ramp to 50% after 48h if no regressions in p99 or token loss.

Open questions for sizing refinement:
1) Can you split the CSV by user-agent (mobile/desktop) and mark which prompts are in the critical vs non-critical bucket?
2) Any plan to increase median response length (you noted max 1024 — do you anticipate shifting median to 256+ in next 6 months?)
3) Do you have a list of 10 highest-traffic prompt templates we should prioritize for KV-cache warming?

If answers are quick I can draft a proposed fleet blueprint (SKU counts, oversubscription, estimated monthly committed cost) by EOD tomorrow.

— Ben
